name: EU DMA alternative payments, links and distribution
plain: In the EU, apps can offer other payment providers and links to the web.
meaning: Brings third party payment and link-out choices to EU users under the Digital Markets Act. Terms include new Apple fees from 2026.

android.permission: Play Console: User choice billing and external offers program for EEA
android.prompt_ui: Play shows user choice or external offers screens
android.store_policy: Play: EEA program terms and service fee tiers
android.api_surface: Alternative billing APIs, external offers for EEA
android.note: Google rolled out EEA programs in 2024 and updated terms in 2025 after DMA scrutiny.

ios.prompt_ui: Apple disclosure sheet when leaving app
ios.store_policy: EU entities only; Core Technology Fee moves to Core Technology Commission Jan 1 2026
ios.api_surface: StoreKit External Purchase, alternative payment service providers
ios.note: Alternative marketplaces and web distribution also EU only.

limits.headline: Can offer other payment providers and web links in the EU, with a clear screen first
limits.user_action: You tap a button that takes you to a payment page or an outside offer
can: Show other payment options or a link to the web in the EU
Show a Play choice or offers screen on Android
Show Apple's disclosure sheet when you leave the app on iPhone
cannot: Do this outside the EU on iPhone, where only the App Store payment is used
Skip the disclosure sheet or choice screen
Offer alternative marketplaces outside the EU
limits.reach_label: A choice you make at checkout
limits.differs: Both only apply in the EU. Google also runs programs in the EEA, and Apple adds a disclosure sheet.

story.what_it_is: In the EU, apps can offer other payment providers and link out to their own website checkout.

marketing.name: Alternative payments in the EU
marketing.pitch: Apple describes the options for EU developers to use other payment providers and link out.

marketing.name: External offers programs
marketing.pitch: Google explains its programs that let some apps offer purchases outside Play Billing.

story.for_you: You may see a screen that says you are leaving the app to pay on a website. It can be cheaper, but you lose the store's refunds and protection.
story.for_makers: Makers can cut store fees and own the customer. Apple warns about scams and fraud, and the terms and fees keep changing.

use_cases.example: A streaming app sends you to its website to subscribe at a lower price.
A game sells currency on its own site with a link from the app.
A store app uses its own payment provider for digital goods.
A dating app offers its own checkout for premium plans.
A news app uses a link out to sell subscriptions.
Fraud teams see more fake pay pages using the same flow.
Marketers can retarget buyers from their own checkout data.

story.android_note: Play shows user choice or external offers screens. Rules changed in 2024 and 2025.
story.ios_note: A disclosure sheet appears when you leave the app. New Apple fees from 2026.

technical_bounds: Region locked; EU storefront and developer entity needed

abuse: Scam and fraud risk Apple cites

history.change: Alternative PSPs, external links, marketplaces in EU
Apple announced new EU terms with a single business model from Jan 2026
User choice billing and external offers extended in EEA
